dedupe_keys.name: community resilience estimates cre for heat

description: The CRE for Heat is an experimental U.S. Census Bureau product, made with Arizona State University's Knowledge Exchange for Resilience, that measures social vulnerability specifically in the context of extreme heat exposure. Whereas the standard Community Resilience Estimates count general disaster risk factors, the heat edition combines American Community Survey microdata and Population Estimates Program data to estimate the share of residents with heat-related risk factors in each area. Coverage: the nation, states, counties and census tracts of the United States; editions for 2019 and 2022 are published as CSV files with file layouts and quick guides. Access: free downloads from the Census Bureau's experimental data products page; public domain. Caveats: it is an experimental product that may not meet all Census Bureau quality standards; estimates are modelled with cross-survey methods, and the two editions are several years apart. The page was last revised on 20 May 2025. Simulation uses: identifying the neighbourhoods where heat waves and power outages during heat events would harm most people, for prioritising cooling centres, grid restoration and heat adaptation planning. Related records: the Community Resilience Estimates, the Local Air Conditioning Estimates (household air-conditioning access, the gap users asked the CRE team to fill), the Household Pulse Survey tables on keeping homes cool, and the FEMA National Risk Index heat wave ratings.
